name: Lights — cctop coach view (toggle c)
principle: Four lights whose glyph (○ quiet, ◐ watch, ● act) you can read from the corner of your eye — each a re-evaluated state tied to one thing you can change (context, cache warmth, limit pace, unverified/contested work) — plus exactly one nudge slot that, in a fixed published order (NOW > NEXT > LATER), names the keystroke, slash command or typed line that resets the light, and retires by itself the moment you do it.

Idle rules: all four glyphs are ○ and uncoloured (absence of colour is the signal). The state line is facts only (last check + last commit), never advice. The slot shows a dim 'quiet' line in the Advisor panel's 'no recommendation right now' style, followed by up to two dim lifecycle rows (acted · <observable completion>, retired · <reason>, expired, snoozed) so the person can see the coach acted-and-vanished rather than went silent; the full lifecycle log is behind 'l'. The cache row shows coarse minutes only — the mm:ss countdown and the 'next' countdown are suppressed while expires_at − now > 300 s (C001). The rework cell flips to 'clean · commit 3m' from the git tick (hidden entirely outside a git repo). 'next' and 'snoozed' show '—'. Without the status-line shim the cache row reads 'warm ≈55m (1h, from last call)' and the limits row '—' (Option in State, never 0 — C041/S03); the agents token is absent when no agent ran.
always_on_numbers: 1. ctx tokens + ▇▁ bar + ≈$/call (context light, e.g. '412k ▇▇▇▇▁▁▁▁▁▁ 41% · ≈$.21/call'; '(cold: next call ≈$2.0)' when prompt_cache.warm is false; 're-reads 412k/call' when $ is toggled to limit units, the default when rate_limits is present — C005/C024). Why: every token added is re-read ~106× and calls above 300k are 25.5 % of calls but 51.6 % of spend (C005); it is the one number the person can move. Source: shim context_window (UNS-13/S01), else the transcript figure labelled 'est'; price = ctx × cache_read from pricing.toml (fable-5-1 0.25 $/MTok) + median output × output price. Bands: ○ < 150k; ◐ 150k–warn band, or ≥ 300k on 1M while a turn runs; ● only when a keystroke changes it now (≥ 300k on 1M with a clean stop available) or ctx ≥ window − 13,000 − 20,000 (BIN-01/C017), never a fixed 80 %. 1-key detail (press 1): 'next 19c ≈$4.4 · fresh ≈$0.9' (session p50 calls per long run × $/call vs the same run at post-/clear ctx p50 45k — Ticker), threshold, +Δ this run, prefix share, 'turn ≈$2.61 ×3.2 7d' from baseline.rs cost_per_turn + multiplier() once ≥ 3 sessions exist (hidden otherwise).

2. cache warmth + time left (cache light, e.g. 'warm 41m (1h)' / 'cold in 4:12 (1h)' / 'cold · 182k re-write' / '—' before the first call). Why: cold calls are 1.8 % of calls but 14.6 % of spend; 55/58 gaps > 60 min were cold (C026); a 1h→5m TTL flip is itself the 'over plan usage' signal (C06). Source: prompt_cache.{warm, ttl, expires_at, recache_tokens_if_cold} in ~/.cctop/status/<sid>.json (S02/F01; C001: trust the shim's TTL), clock-driven from expires_at because the file rewrites only at expiry; fallback last_line_at_ms + agg.observed_ttl marked ≈ and ignored when the file is older than the last assistant line; mm:ss only under 5 min (2 min on 5m). 1-key detail (2): hit ratio, misses this session with last named cause and re-written tokens, TTL source, 'misses 3 · 2.9M tok · $6.10 · idle 1 · rebuilds 1'.

3. 5h limit % + reset, with the agents token (limits light, e.g. '5h 62% · ↻ 2h10 · agents 3 run · 86%'). Why: for a subscriber the plan window is the real budget (all 8 local status files carry rate_limits) and only 4 rate-limit hits happened in a month, so the pain is headroom; subagent spend is 13.7 % of the corpus and 86 % of this session yet invisible today (C014). Source: rate_limits.five_hour from the shim ('—' when absent, S03); 7d in the same cell only when ≥ 60 %; ◐ when A13's least-squares exhaustion lands before resets_at or 5h ≥ 80 %, ● on a rate_limit/spend_limit error line (C060). Agents from a recursive scan of <session>/subagents/** (GAP-01) + SubagentStart/SubagentStop registration, agents whose only assistant line is <synthetic> excluded and counted as 'failed'; token shown only while an agent runs or share ≥ 25 %. 1-key detail (3): 7d %, other live sessions on the window, exhaustion fit, 'agents ≈$897 (86 %) · 90 ran · 174 failed (spend limit)', rate-limit weights fable 10 / opus 5 / sonnet 3 / haiku 1.

4. edits since last check + age of last check, streak prepended (rework light, e.g. 'edits 3 ✓ none 11m' / '3 fails ▸gh pr view · edits 3 ✓ none 11m' / 'edits 0 · ✓ 6m ago · clean · commit 3m'). Why: 41 % of source-edit turns end unverified and 13/15 stay unverified next turn, while verified episodes reach a check in p50 2 calls / 31 s (C030); 5.1 % of Bash calls fail and 29 blind same-prefix retries/month follow (C037); the uncommitted tail is the blast radius a rewind or bad commit puts at risk (C032). Source: Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit and implement-class Bash on non-doc paths since the last test-class Bash whose stdout confirmed a run ('test result:'/'passed'/'failed', is_error for fail — C055 test vs build/lint split); doc-only edits (.md/.txt/.json/.yaml/.toml/.csv, 69 % of edit turns) count 0; fails = consecutive non-denial is_error in the last 10 calls sharing a normalised 40-char prefix (denials counted apart, C038/C050); uncommitted from the 5-s git tick (numstat vs current HEAD, porcelain count, HEAD sha resets the counter). ◐ at > 10 min or ≥ 14 calls since first edit (p90), 2 shared-prefix fails, a PR open without review, or the commit tail; ● on cascade, denial streak, correction streak, destructive git on a dirty tree, commit without check, or turn end with unverified src edits and a known test command. 1-key detail (4): last check command + result, 'fails N ▸prefix / denied M' with error classes this turn, 'uncommitted +412 −87 · 9 files · 18 edits · 42m', rewind checkpoints since the last prompt.

5. run size and silence (state line, e.g. '18c +42k · silent 3:50 · nudged 2×', or '▸ steer window' on calls 1–5). Why: it is the Esc-or-wait decision number — interrupts cluster at p50 3 calls in (PH-14), runs > 20 calls end in text 96 % but 62 % contain a tool error (C023), so the person should watch the rework light, not the clock. Source: API calls and usage.input deltas since the last non-empty assistant text block; attachment silent_turn_reminder count (6/11/16/21 calls, model/version gated — 'nudged N×' omitted when absent); batching_reminder_sent is not used (fires on every post-tool call). Deliberately a state, not a light.

6. phase word + churn token (state line, e.g. 'IMPLEMENTING · render.rs ×5', 'EXPLORING · 8 reads', '◆ WAITING 4m · Claude asked a question (2 options)', 'IDLE 4m · cargo test ok 6m ago · committed 3m ago', 'LOOP · stop hook re-fed prompt 44×'). Why: it tells the person what kind of moment this is before any number is read, and the churn token (one file edited ≥ 4× this turn with interleaved re-reads: 37 turn/file cases, 67 edit→read→edit sequences in the corpus) is the earliest visible sign of a wrong direction. Source: tool names only (Edit/Write/implement-class Bash → IMPLEMENTING; Read/Grep/Glob/read-only Bash → EXPLORING; Agent → EXPLORING (delegated); AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode pending or Notification idle_prompt/permission_prompt → WAITING; end_turn + ≥ 60 s → IDLE; C058 loop signature → LOOP); a check is always quoted literally ('cargo test ok 6m ago'), never an inferred VERIFYING word (47–56 % verify agreement, C041/C055); files.rs per-file counters for churn.
nudge_model:
SUBSTRATE. `cctop query coach` (C064) is one pure function of State returning {state:{word, churn_file, run_calls, run_dctx, silent_ms, nudged, steer_window, waiting_on, session_mode}, lights:[{id, level:0|1|2, number, detail, source:{shim|hooks|transcript|git}, approx}×4], agents:{running, share, failed}, nudge:{id, family, class, line1, line2, evidence, action_text, action_kind: prompt|slash|setting|key, since_turn, retires_on, acted, acting}, next:{id, text, fires_when}, snoozed:[{id, until_turn|session}], recent:[{at, kind: fired|acted|expired|retired|snoozed, id, completion}], suppressed:[{id, reason}]}. The verb truncates line1/line2 to 52 cells (51 render inside the 56-col frame; the pane and skill get the same strings), so all surfaces render identically. Advice (src/advisor/mod.rs) gains class, family, since_turn, retires_on, acted, acting; engine state persists to ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json with a single writer (the TUI while running, else the CLI/MCP caller) guarded by a lock file so the 2-s pane poller never races the TUI. Every number carries source and approx; a missing source renders '—', never 0.

LIGHTS ARE STATES, NOT MESSAGES. A light's level is a predicate re-evaluated every tick and never rate-limited; it says nothing, so it cannot nag. When a nudge is snoozed or retired its light keeps its level: a red light with an empty slot means 'you told me to be quiet about this'. Level 2 (●) is reserved for 'a keystroke changes this now' — the context light is ● only with a clean stop available or inside the binary's warn band, so a deliberate 1M session sits amber, not red all day. The rework cell always keeps 'edits N ✓ age'; streaks are prepended.

ONE SLOT, FIXED ORDER. Exactly one nudge (headline / action / evidence row); one 'next' row holding the highest-ranked queued nudge with the condition that promotes it; one 'snoozed' row. Classes strictly pre-empt: NOW (act within this turn) > NEXT (act at the next boundary) > LATER (turn-end retrospective). Within a class the order is fixed and published — not tokens × remaining calls, which would bury rework nudges (all three judges): NOW: turn-died > waiting-on-you > cache-countdown > failure-cascade > denial-streak > correction-streak > commit-without-check > destructive-git > warm-switch-undo > double-steer. NEXT: cold-resume > verify-gap > context-reset > post-compaction > loop-armed > review-before-merge > commit-tail > explore-delegate > cold-switch-hint. LATER: named cache miss > agent-context-heavy > screenshot-heavy > prefix-tip. Re-fires of one family (context +100k steps) rank newest first. Promotion happens only when the occupant retires or a higher class arrives; a same-class newcomer waits in 'next'. Two rules are next-row-only, never the slot, never a toast: plan-first and instruction-drift (prior-based, no measured precision).

ADMISSION BAR (Phase Coach's 4-in-5 rule, made concrete). A rule may take the slot only if its trigger is structural (isApiErrorMessage line, AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode without result, Notification type, is_error ×3 with shared prefix, top-level toolDenialKind, '[Request interrupted' text, compact_boundary, diagnostics.cache_miss_reason, git-tick numbers, session_crons, PreModelSwitch or a history.jsonl /model row, prompt_cache.expires_at) or its corpus precision is ≥ 4 in 5 in the verdicts (switch-warm 10/10, review-before-merge 60/81, cold-resume 55/58, boundary '?' 89 %). Anything resting on the Bash phase classifier's verify class (verify-gap's ✓ reset, commit-without-check) uses only the test-class pattern with stdout confirmation until the ~200-call hand-label pass (C041/C055); explore-delegate counts only Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch plus a narrow read-only Bash allowlist (cat, ls, rg/grep, find, head/tail, sed -n, git log/show/diff/status).

PHASE GATE (eligibility filter, not a displayed word). verify-gap: never while the last call is test-class; context-reset and checkpoint: only after a clean end_turn text with no background work; waiting-on-you and cache-countdown: only while idle; cascade, denial, double-steer, destructive-git: only in a running turn; commit-without-check: on the commit result; LATER rules: only at turn end or session start. Phase words come from tool names only.

RETIREMENT — each nudge names all three: (a) predicate false (the light it cites dropped — this is why the lights exist); (b) acted: one observable completion per rule (a test-class Bash or a Read of a file edited this turn; a new assistant line / API call; a new transcript file or SessionStart source=clear; a successful call of the failing prefix or the rule appearing in permissions.allow; a review Skill/Agent marker or merge; HEAD sha change; an Agent tool_use; the next human prompt where nothing else is observable); (c) hard TTL: NOW at turn end (turn_duration/Stop) — NOW rules that fire at turn end live until the next human prompt; NEXT at the next human prompt; LATER after 3 human turns. Enter puts the nudge in an 'acting' state: it shows 'acting…' until its acted predicate fires, logs 'acted · <completion>' to recent (idle view shows the last two), or 'expired' when the TTL wins — so a fooled coach is visible. Human turn = promptSource ∈ {typed, suggestion_accepted, queued} or origin.kind == human (C057; the current heuristic over-counts 20 %).

ANTI-FLICKER, BUDGET, COOLDOWN, SNOOZE. The slot occupant changes only at a human-turn boundary, on a NOW event, or when the occupant retires — never on a render tick (Ticker). Budget in human turns, not wall-clock: ≤ 1 newly promoted nudge per human turn; ≤ 3 distinct nudges in any 10 human turns; ≤ 1 LATER per 2 human turns; a same-family re-fire counts. Per-rule cooldown 5 human turns after retirement (10 for correction streak). 'Shown' counts once per human turn in which the nudge held the slot; a nudge shown 3 human turns unacted self-snoozes for the session (Claude Code's own tip cooldownSessions pattern, X01). x = snooze 5 turns (a third snooze of the same rule = rest of session), X = snooze for the session; both persist so query/pane/skill agree.

SUPPRESSION. session_mode (C058): loop when the last 2 stop_hook_summary lines have hookErrors non-empty or a hook_blocking_error with hookEvent==Stop appears in the last 3 turns and no typed prompt since → the slot holds only the loop-health indicator; machine when the last prompt is promptSource system/sdk or origin.kind task-notification; team when agent-setting lines or teamName exist (no /clear or reply advice). bridge-session/entrypoint are not gates. Subagent transcripts never feed nudges. NEXT/LATER are silent for the first 2 human turns and after > 2 h away (cold-resume is the one NEXT exception); NOW is exempt (13/14 rate-limit errors land on a session's first call). Never duplicate Claude Code's own footer: no pre-compaction countdown ('% until auto-compact' exists; A06 gets the '/compact <focus> while warm' wording), no auto-continue echo, no effort-downgrade echo, no warm-/model confirm; a single queued steer is a state-line token. <synthetic>/isApiErrorMessage lines produce only turn-died and are excluded from context, velocity, model and compaction math (C017).

EVIDENCE NEXT TO ADVICE. Every nudge's numbers come from a light or the state line already on screen; 'e' opens the explain overlay with evidence lines and metric ids, the acted predicate, corpus rate ('right 10/10 last month · fires ~15×/month'), the priced saving and its stated assumption ('saves ≈3× assumes sonnet at the same tool count'), the doc_key, and the last 3 retired nudges with reason.

AUDIT + A01–A18 RESOLUTION. Every fire/acted/expired/snooze is an Events row kind=coach; priced events (cache miss with cause + $, cold write, agent batch, top-5 % turn, model switch, loop fires, API error, compaction — ≥ 20k tokens or ≥ $0.10) are Events rows kind=cost (Ticker's tape lives on the dashboard, not here); the SessionEnd report tallies 'nudges: 7 fired, 4 acted, 2 snoozed'. Overlaps are resolved, not layered: A01 → named-miss's fallback only; A02 → ledger post-mortem (cold-resume owns timing); A03 gains the persistedOutputPath line; A05 → explore-delegate (Bash-aware); A06 reworded (pre-compaction half of C018); A09 → denial-streak (never bare Bash); A13 stays as the limits light; A14 → agent-context-heavy; A15 subsumed by failure-cascade; A18 → context-reset. The dashboard's Advisor panel shows the coach's primary nudge as its first row so the two views never disagree.

These lines are excluded from model adoption, velocity, context and compaction detection (8 of 8 current 'compactions' are these zero-usage lines).

risks:
1. Verify classification is the weak link for the two most valuable rework nudges: the Bash phase classifier agrees with the model's own description only 47–56 % for 'verify' (C041/C055). Baked-in mitigation: the rework light's ✓ resets only on a test-class command whose stdout confirms a run (or is_error); IMPLEMENTING/EXPLORING come from tool names only; VERIFY is quoted literally; verify-gap and commit-without-check escalate on the phase word only after the ~200-call hand-labelled sample; until then ambiguous write+run commands are labelled verify so the nudges err to silence.

2. Data prerequisites are real work and nothing fires correctly without them: C055 classifier with the full Bash command (tools.rs clips to 30 chars; hooks.rs:75 strips tool_input), C056/C057 ingestion (toolUseResult, top-level toolDenialKind/userFeedback/interruptedMessageId, promptSource/origin, attachment subtypes, Stop payload), C017's synthetic filter (8 of 8 current 'compactions' are zero-usage error lines and '<synthetic>' is adopted as the model), UNS-13 prompt_cache parsing, GAP-01 recursive agent scan (66 % of workflow agents are failed '<synthetic>' spawns), C032's git-tick rewrite (numstat vs current HEAD), the Advice fields and persisted advisor.json (C062/C064), C058 session_mode and C057 turn identity (the current heuristic over-counts human turns 20 %, so cooldowns and budgets count wrong turns until it lands; Ralph loops would otherwise receive 'reply with…' nudges into an empty terminal — the fastest way to train the person to ignore the view). Shipping the view first would put the old A01–A18 predicates in a new frame.

3. Source availability differs per install: without the status shim the cache light falls back to last call + observed TTL (marked ≈, wrong across a 1h→5m flip until the next call) and limits shows '—'; without `cctop install` there is no permission_pending, Stop.background_tasks, session_crons, Notification type or PreModelSwitch — waiting-on-you rests on transcript pairing, context-reset loses its 'no background work' gate (pendingBackgroundAgentCount omitted when 0 and missing for 1/3 of turns), the warm-switch nudge becomes a post-hoc undo window from history.jsonl; 0 of 42 local SessionStart events were resume/fork so cold-resume's hook path is unverified. Every light must render '—' and label estimates, or the numbers lie in exactly the sessions that need coaching.

4. Dollars are notional for this subscriber (all 8 status files carry rate_limits): `$` defaults to limit units there, but the /usage weighting (cached + uncached×10 + cacheCreate×12.5 + output×50 × model tier) is not reproduced, so '≈$0.21/call' and 'next 19c ≈$4.4' can mislead about plan usage; fable-5-1's 0.025× cache read makes the ctx lever 4× weaker than on opus-5, so per-model prices from pricing.toml, never a rule of thumb; the per-call price is valid only warm — after a TTL flip or cold gap the tile must say '(cold: next call ≈$2.0)' or it under-prices the next step 10–20×; the '×N 7d' multiplier needs ≥ 3 sessions (MIN_TURNS) and hides otherwise.

5. Band thresholds (150k/300k on 1M windows, warn band window−13k−20k) are tuned on one month / 113 transcripts of one user; the effective auto-compact window can be lowered server-side or by CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW / CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE (read via ps eww), so the context light must mirror Claude Code's own '% of window' when the window is not exact and never claim 'N turns until autocompact'; the 'clean stop' gate that keeps the context light amber mid-turn means a person who never lets a turn end cleanly sees ◐ forever — accepted, because the alternative is a red light all day.

6. One slot hides a second simultaneous problem; the lights, the 'next' row with its firing condition and the '+N queued (n)' counter are the mitigation, but a person who never presses n or 1-4 sees only the top nudge. The fixed intra-class order is a design choice (predictability over measured optimality); tokens × calls survives only as a tie-break.

7. Acted predicates can misfire (a test run for another reason retires verify-gap; an Agent spawned for another reason retires explore-delegate; a Read of an edited file 'verifies'; a HEAD change from an outside commit retires commit-tail; a new transcript file from an unrelated /clear retires context-reset) and cooldowns can hide a genuinely repeated problem; both are accepted because the light keeps its level, 'acted · <completion>' is visible in the idle rows and lifecycle log, and the Events audit trail records every fire/acted/expired/snooze for later tuning.

8. Explore-delegate's evidence has an open question (the 'Explore agent returns p50 71 tok' figure may be a truncated toolUseResult) and its honest mid-run action costs the cut turn; it is NEXT, never a toast, and gated on a narrow read-only allowlist — but it is the one grafted nudge whose benefit is inferred from the phase model rather than a verified candidate, like commit-without-check (32 % unchecked commits from the phase model, not a verdict). Both start slot-eligible only via structural triggers and should be the first rules re-examined against the Events tally.

9. The 'S' send-over-socket path in the ask popup is the only channel that writes into the session; it is pre-existing (ask.rs), restricted to prompt-class actions, and arrives as a message at the next call (tokens then) — still, it must stay opt-in-per-press and never default, or FR-15's read-only stance is compromised in spirit; the pane never gets an equivalent.

10. Rendering: ○ ◐ ● ◆ ▸ ↻ ✓ ▇ ▁ are East-Asian-ambiguous-width glyphs (same class as the existing ◆ ■ ▸ ─ │ ·), so terminals set to ambiguous=wide will misalign rows — a theme-level ASCII fallback (o / + / * / # / _) must exist as it does for the border set; OSC 52 clipboard is blocked in some terminals (Apple Terminal) so Enter falls back to pbcopy/xclip and, failing that, shows the text selectable in the popup.

11. The persisted ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json introduces a writer race between the TUI, the 2-s pane poller and MCP callers; the single-writer rule (TUI owns the file while running; CLI writes only when no TUI lock exists) must be implemented with a lock file or snooze/since_turn state will flap across surfaces.

12. Frequency is low and skewed by design: cold-countdown realistically catches 2–4 events/month, post-compaction ~1 per 113 sessions, warm-switch ~1 per 11 sessions, correction-streak 3–8/month, destructive git ~0.5/day, while three sessions carry 83 % of the context saving — the view will look quiet most of the time and its value is dominated by four families (verify gap, context reset, waiting-on-you, failure cascade/denials); the idle lifecycle rows and the SessionEnd tally are what make quiet look like working rather than broken.
